entityDescription:
Rzeszow University of Technology (RUT), named after Ignacy Łukasiewicz, is a leading technical university in southeastern Poland. Established in 1951, it currently educates over 11,200 students across 7 faculties and plays a key role in Poland’s aerospace and innovation ecosystem.

Aviation and Space Competences

RUT was the first university in Poland to educate civil aviation pilots through an academic program. Its Aviation Training Centre in Jasionka and Gliding Centre in Bezmiechowa combine advanced pilot training with applied aerospace research.

The Faculty of Mechanical Engineering and Aeronautics houses:

- Department of Aerospace Engineering – focusing on aerodynamics, structures, propulsion, UAVs, and hybrid systems;

- Department of Avionics and Control – developing flight control, navigation, and autonomous aircraft technologies;

- Laboratories for aerospace structures and materials, including hydrogen combustion and fatigue testing.

RUT is involved in major R&D initiatives related to hybrid and hydrogen propulsion, fuel cells, and flight tests with alternative-energy platforms.

Scientific and Industrial Focus

Key research areas include Mechanical Engineering and Materials Engineering, supported by doctoral programs and active industry collaboration. Topics range from machine design and robotics to space-grade materials.

RUT coordinates the AERONET–Aviation Valley Center, connecting 12 Polish universities and institutes to deliver innovation to the national aerospace sector.

Future Vision

RUT aims to:

- Lead in European aerospace and engineering education,

- Expand hydrogen and electric aviation technologies,

- Enhance technology transfer and university-industry collaboration across advanced manufacturing and aerospace sector,

- Advance space-related R&D, including material testing under ECSS, small satellite systems, and UAV-based high-altitude platforms,

- Be a central player in Poland’s and CEE’s space economy development.

The transformation of the food industry has a significant impact on mitigating the climate crisis. The consumption of regionally and locally produced food from farms is a central 'lever' for the economical, ecological and social sustainability transformation of the food system. However, systematic cooperation between small farms and the large chains of food retail, which would pay off enormously, is currently prevented by structural differences between the supply and demand sides.
In detail, this is due to the following:
1.The core competence of agricultural producers is the production of food, rather than its professional marketing in food retailing.
2.Although local products in the product portfolio are highly attractive for food retailers, the high coordination and transaction costs associated with the large number of small suppliers, together with their incompatibility with the logistics systems of EDEKA, REWE, Globus, etc. prevent them from being offered.
 
LOKORA addresses this constellation with its innovative business model withthe help of the following core elements:
1.A unique transaction and collaboration platform enables efficient communication between market participants, the processing of the transactions,field quality analysis and demand forecasting based on satellite data as well as the scale-oriented bundling of supply and actual demand.
2.With the help of machine learning approaches, an intelligent, platform-based micrologistics system ensures resource-optimized, decentrally organized direct deliveries to food retail outlets with GNSS based real-time fleet management of e-delivery vans, thus redefining local value chains in a multinational scalable way.
3.An integrated range of services in the areas of logistics, sales and marketing.

DRONE VOLT founded in 2011 is an international reference group specializing in the development of new aerial technologies, more particularly in civil drones manufacturing and embedded artificial intelligence.
Three brands are brought together within the DRONE VOLT Group: DRONE VOLT aeronautical manufacturer and expert in professional civil drones. AERIALTRONICS specialized in artificial intelligence and DANDRONE online DJI drones and multi-brand accessories distributor for civil and commercial applications.
The leading brand DRONE VOLT designs and manufactures commercial drones in its two production centers based in France and in the Netherlands for various civilian applications in the energy, construction, security and agricultural sectors.
The Group, led by Stefano Valentini, employs around fifty people in France and abroad: Belgium, Denmark, the Netherlands, Switzerland, the US and Canada.
With its technical expertise and experience, DRONE VOLT offers industries global solutions including associated services but also more specific solutions such as the development of custom drone projects with our engineering consulting and design office, aerial data acquisition services, professional drone training with DRONE VOLT ACADEMY, assistance, maintaining and legal support.
DRONE VOLT listed on the Euronext Growth market in Paris provides UAVs to various administrations and industrial groups such as the French Army, the Ministry of the Armed Forces, Airbus, Engie, Total, RTE, Bouygues ES, ADP, the Gendarmerie des Transports Aériens (GTA) and international government agencies.
Our drones are based on more sustainable electrical technology. They generate 0% CO2 and thus help reduce the environmental impact of our partners.
DRONE VOLT is qualified as an “Innovative Company” by Bpifrance.
Our Philosophy
At Dronevolt, we don't build drones, we build flying tools.
We understand that drones are often associated with recreational or military activities, but at Dronevolt our goal is to design flying tools that can be used in professional applications. We believe drones can be used to improve business operations and industries by providing unique insights and automating dangerous or difficult tasks.
Our drones are designed to be reliable, robust and suitable for harsh environments. They are equipped with advanced technologies such as automatic stabilization, GPS navigation, high resolution camera and real-time data transmission. These features allow users to perform high-quality inspections, accurate mappings and real-time monitoring of their business activities.
We also collaborate with companies and organizations to develop customized solutions that meet the specific needs of our customers. We have previously worked with companies in the oil and gas industry, renewable energy companies, environmental organizations and emergency services to help them improve their operational efficiency and reduce their environmental impact.
At Dronevolt, we build disruptive technologies that will change the paradigm of many industries and activities to methods that are more environmentally friendly and safer for human operators. Our goal is to disrupt traditional helicopter missions in many of these activities.
We believe our disruptive technology can play a key role in the transition to a more sustainable and environmentally friendly economy. We are convinced that drones can become an essential tool in many fields and we are determined to continue our mission to make them more accessible and more efficient for companies and end users.

The CERAU, Centre d'Etudes et de Recherches d'Architecture et d'Urbanisme (ww.cerau.com) was established in 1968 as de-facto association. In 1980, the CERAU transformed its legal status to become a private limited company (SPRL). 
The partners have organized a collective leadership ensuring, through the contribution of the personality and skills of each architect, the company’s efficiency and creativity.
The CERAU is currently run by three managing partners architects Cestmira VESELA, Rémy RASCOL, Aleksander PRIFTI and recently extended the partnership to two younger architects.
Besides the partners architects and urban-planners, the CERAU team is made up of more or less twenty people. The employees are divided into teams around a project manager and under the leadership of the partners architects. The partners contribute to the training of the younger architects and architects-interns, by offering young colleagues varied and creative activity in the studio. 
 
CERAU’s activity extends from designing architecture projects to the mission of construction management and the acceptance of completed works. It encompasses all the analyses, surveys, developments in urban planning and land use planning. It also covers the areas of industrialization, decoration and layout of outdoor spaces.
The diversity of the projects treated go from specific urban and regional planning studies to the interiors through the full range of architectural tasks relating to housing, office space, industry and equipment.

Pilotage
The CERAU has many years of solid experience in terms of steering groups of architects. Achievements such as the European Parliament and the La Plaine office complex or ongoing housing projects such as Tivoli Green City and the Alliance residential park.
 
Sustainability and energy saving
The CERAU has extensive practice in energy efficiency for buildings and master the regulations of the Brussels region. To cite only the most illustrative projects, the Bridge Building part of the Porte d’Ostende complex in Berchem -Saint -Agathe, was the first BREEAM certified office building in Belgium, Ateliers Mommaerts et Choux de Bruxelles projects were labeled "BATEX" (exemplary Buildings) by IBGE and the SIBELGA project, one of the first "passive" office spaces in the Brussels region. In terms of housing, our many references include the new Tivoli sustainable neighborhood in Laeken (Brussels) where all the housing units are “passive” and about 30% of them are “zero energy” and the Alliance residential park in Braine-l'Alleud (Wallonia) where the apartments are either "low energy" or "passive". Recently, the Tivoli Green City project obtained the Belgian Environment and Energy award for 2018.
 
BIM
The CERAU has acquired the necessary tools to develop its projects following the BIM method (Building Information Modeling) that integrates in a single database, all the buildings’ architectural parameters; technical, descriptive, and quantitative, throughout their life cycle, from their creation to their destruction.

▪ BECI|Brussels Enterpr. Commerce & Industry|www.beci.be

entityName: AECSIC - Instituto de Microelectronica de Sevilla
entityDescription:
The Institute is dedicated to the field of Physical Science and Technologies, one of the eight areas into which research activity is divided by the CSIC. Its main area of specialization is the design and testing of analog and mixed-signal integrated circuits in CMOS technology, as well as their use in different application contexts such as biomedical devices, wireless communications, data conversion, smart imagers & vision sensors, cybersecurity, neuromorphic computing and space technology.
The IMSE-CNM began its operations in October 1989 under the auspices of an agreement signed by the Junta de Andalucía (the Andalusian Regional Government), the CSIC and the Universidad de Sevilla. Its founding research group was initially based on the premises of the Centro de Informática Científica de Andalucía (CICA – Scientific Computing Center of Andalucía), as a subsidiary department of the Instituto de Microelectrónica de Barcelona (Barcelona Institute of Microelectronics). Later, in 1996, it was established by the Governing Board of the CSIC as a Institute in Formation, occupying a building next to the CICA ceded by the Junta de Andalucía. In late 2008, the Institute was enlarged and relocated in new premises purpose-built by the CSIC in the Parque Científico y Tecnológico Cartuja (Cartuja Scientific and Technological Park). On October 2015, by means of a Specific Collaboration Agreement signed by the CSIC and the Universidad de Sevilla, the center became a Joint Institute of both institutions.
The IMSE-CNM staff consists of approximately one hundred people, including scientists and support personnel. Most of them work for the CSIC and the Universidad de Sevilla. IMSE-CNM employees are involved in advancing scientific knowledge, designing high level scientific-technical solutions and in technology transfer. Their duties include both research and teaching activities, the latter mainly at official master and PhD degrees.
The projects undertaken at the Institute mostly correspond to EU research initiatives, National R+D Plans and Research Plans funded by the Junta de Andalucía. They focus primarily on implementing innovative concepts in silicon, using either the CNM's own clean room at the Instituto de Microelectrónica de Barcelona (IMB-CNM) or external foundries, mainly from Europractice or CMP IC services.
The Institute also participates in several technology and knowledge transfer activities with microelectronics companies, at both national and international level. These activities take the form of collaboration in numerous research contracts, the organization of training courses and the provision of scientific and technical consultation services for companies and government departments.

High Precision Capillary Printing (HPCAP) is the smallest fountain pen in the world: a unique additive manufacturing technology invented by Hummink. Inspired by atomic force microscopy, it exploits the strength of capillary forces to print any ink on any substrate with resolutions ranging from 100 nm to tens of microns and an unprecedented positioning precision. HPCAP doesn’t require external source of pressure, voltage, or UV, hence alleviating common issues of printing technologies such as satellite drops or material limitations.
HPCAP bridges the resolution gap between lithography and more conventional additive manufacturing (i.e: inkjet printing) to address state-of-the-art challenges in the fields of semiconductor and printed electronics.
